topology: 1 node x 1 H100 used (of 4), ONE process, no MPI
why: a cudaMalloc has to be an object whichever provider ran (PLAN-20261118-1930). Until the engine observed the driver's allocation family, only gpumem (NVBit) recorded plain device allocations, so every MPI science-app capture (LAMMPS, QE, GROMACS over UCX) had an empty mem_object while its sends named GPU buffers by address. This case drives every route by which a program gets CUDA memory — the runtime (built static AND shared), the driver linked -lcuda, the driver by dlsym, VMM maps — and asserts each produced exactly its object, from a provider (-p cupti) that records no objects of its own.
why_no_goldens: every route allocates at a size no other route uses, all fixed by params, so each claim is an assertion that finds its object by (origin, size) — no address, no id.
found_note: the case's three behaviours are the three ways the doors could be wrong while every route still 'works': a double free emitting two closes, one cuMemUnmap closing the wrong mappings (or none), and an allocate/free loop recording one open per call but never its close.
workload_note: sizes are 3 MiB + k * 4 KiB, distinct per route and far from anything a runtime allocates for itself. The workload allocates every route's buffer and keeps them all live, runs the loop, then frees everything but the managed buffer — so no two routes can ever share an address, and therefore an interned id.
